children.translated_text: Having returned from his teacher's household, he should support his mother and father.

children.text: tābhyām anujñāto bhāryām upayacchet sajātāṃ nagnikāṃ brahmacāriṇīm asagotrām ||
children.translated_text: With their permission he should marry a wife: of the same class, not previously given to another man, a brahmacāriṇī, and not of the same <s>gotra</s>.

children.text: ahnaḥ pañcasu kāleṣu prātaḥ saṃgave madhyaṃdine 'parāhṇe sāyaṃ vaiteṣu yatkārī syāt puṇyāha eva kurute ||
children.translated_text: At any of the five times of the day, morning, forenoon, midday, afternoon, or evening, whatever action he performs, he performs on an auspicious day.

children.text: agnim upasamādhāya paridhānāntaṃ kṛtvā vadhūm ānīyamānāṃ samīkṣate
children.translated_text: Having placed the fire, and having completed the rite up to the enclosing-sticks, he looks at the bride as she is being brought forward:

children.text: sumaṅgalīr iyaṃ vadhūr imāṃ sameta paśyata
children.translated_text: 'This bride is auspicious. Come together and look upon her.
Having bestowed good fortune upon her, go back each to your own house.'
So the formula runs.
The wife sits down to the right of her husband.
When she has sipped water and has been touched, he sprinkles around, as before.
Having performed the rite up to the <s>vyāhṛti</s> formulas, he offers oblations:

children.text: agnir aitu prathamo devatānāṃ so 'syai prajāṃ muñcatu mṛtyupāśāt
children.translated_text: 'Let <s>Agni</s>, first among the deities, come; let him release offspring for her from the noose of death.

children.text: tad ayaṃ rājā varuṇo 'numanyatāṃ yatheyaṃ strī pautram aghaṃ na rodāt
children.translated_text: Let this king <s>Varuṇa</s> consent, so that this woman may not weep over the misfortune of a grandson.'
'Svāhā.'

children.text: imām agnis trāyatāṃ gārhapatyaḥ prajām asyai nayatu dīrgham āyuḥ
children.translated_text: 'Let this <s>Agni Gārhapatya</s> protect her; let him lead offspring to long life for her.

children.text: aśūnyopasthā jīvatām astu mātā pautram ānandam abhiprabudhyatām iyam
children.translated_text: Let the mother live with her lap not empty; let this woman awaken to the joy of a grandson.'
'Svāhā.'

children.text: mā te gṛhe niśi ghoṣa utthād anyatra tvad rudatyaḥ saṃviśantu
children.translated_text: 'May no cry arise in your house at night; let women who weep lie down elsewhere than with you.

children.text: mā tvaṃ vikeśy ura āvadhiṣṭhā jīvapatnī patiloke virāja prajāṃ paśyantī sumanasyamānām
children.translated_text: Do not, with disheveled hair, strike your breast. With your husband alive, shine in your husband's world, seeing your offspring and rejoicing.'
'Svāhā.'

children.text: dyaus te pṛṣṭhaṃ rakṣatu vāyur ūrū aśvinau ca stanaṃ dhayatas te putrān savitābhirakṣatu
children.translated_text: 'Let <s>Dyauḥ</s> protect your back, <s>Vāyu</s> your thighs, and the two <s>Aśvins</s> your breast; let <s>Savitṛ</s> protect your sons as they drink.

children.text: ā vāsasaḥ paridhānād bṛhaspatir viśve devā abhirakṣantu paścāt
children.translated_text: From the putting on of the garment let <s>Bṛhaspati</s> protect you, and let all the gods protect you from behind.'
'Svāhā.'
'Childlessness, death of a grandson, evil, or misfortune,

children.text: śīrṣṇaḥ srajam ivonmucya dviṣadbhyaḥ pratimuñcāmi pāpam
children.translated_text: as one removes a garland from the head, I remove evil and fasten it upon the enemies.'
'Svāhā.'

children.text: devakṛtaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ kalpamānaṃ tena hanmi yoniṣadaḥ piśācān
children.translated_text: 'With this god-made, brahman-forming rite I strike down the <s>piśācas</s> that sit in the womb.

children.text: kravyādo mṛtyūn adharān pādayāmi dīrgham āyus tava jīvantu putrāḥ
children.translated_text: I cast the flesh-eating deaths downward; may your sons live a long life.'
'Svāhā.'
So the formulas run.
After offering 'This of mine, O <s>Varuṇa</s>,'
'To you I go,'
'You, O <s>Agni</s>, for us,'
'So you, O <s>Agni</s>, for us,'
'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the expiation,'
and '<s>Prajāpati</s>,'
he sets her upon a stone.

children.text: ātiṣṭhemam aśmānam aśmeva tvaṃ sthirā bhava
children.translated_text: 'Step upon this stone; be firm like a stone.
Crush the assailants; overpower those who fight against you.'
So the formula runs.

children.text: apareṇāgniṃ dvayān darbhān pūrvāparān udagagrān saṃstīrya teṣu pūrvāparāv avatiṣṭhete ||
children.translated_text: West of the fire he spreads two darbha grasses, lying east-west and with their tips to the north, and on them the two stand facing east and west.

children.text: prāṅmukhaḥ pratyaṅmukhyā hastaṃ gṛhṇīyāt pratyaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukhyā vā
children.translated_text: Facing east he should take the hand of her who faces west, or facing west that of her who faces east.

children.text: yadi kāmayeta puṃso janayeyam ity aṅguṣṭhaṃ gṛhṇīyāt
children.translated_text: If he wishes, 'May I beget a male,' he should grasp the thumb.
If he wishes, 'Females,' he should grasp the fingers.

children.text: yadi kāmayetobhayaṃ janayeyam ity abhīva lomāny aṅguṣṭhaṃ sahāṅgulibhir gṛhṇīyāt
children.translated_text: If he wishes, 'May I beget both,' he should grasp the hair-side, the thumb together with the fingers.

children.text: sarasvati predam iva subhage vājinīvati tāṃ tvā viśvasya bhūtasya prajāyām asy agrataḥ
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, go forth here, as it were, blessed one, rich in strength; you are foremost in the offspring of all being.

children.text: gṛhṇāmi te suprajāstvāya hastaṃ mayā patyā jaradaṣṭir yathāsat
children.translated_text: I take your hand for good offspring, so that you may grow old with me as your husband.

children.text: bhago 'ryamā savitā puraṃdhir mahyaṃ tvādur gārhapatyāya devāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Puraṃdhi</s>, and the gods have given you to me for the household fire.'
So the formula runs.

children.text: tām agreṇa dakṣiṇam aṃsaṃ pratīcīm abhyāvṛtyābhimantrayate
children.translated_text: Turning her back around her right shoulder from the front, he addresses her:

children.text: aghoracakṣur apatighny edhi śivā paśubhyaḥ sumanāḥ suvarcāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Be of kindly gaze, not killing your husband; be gracious to the cattle, well-disposed, and full of good brilliance.

children.text: jīvasūr vīrasūḥ syonā śaṃ na edhi dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade
children.translated_text: Bearing living children, bearing heroic sons, kindly be auspicious for our bipeds and auspicious for our quadrupeds.

children.text: tāṃ naḥ pūṣan śivatamāmerayasva yasyāṃ bījaṃ manuṣyā vapanti
children.translated_text: O <s>Pūṣan</s>, set her most auspiciously in motion for us, in whom men sow seed.

children.text: yā na ūrū uśatī viśrayātai yasyām uśantaḥ praharema śepam
children.translated_text: She who, desiring, spreads her thighs for us, in whom we, desiring, shall thrust the member.

children.text: somaḥ prathamo vivide gandharvo vivida uttaraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s> first obtained her; the <s>Gandharva</s> obtained her next.
<s>Agni</s> was your third husband; I, born among men, am the fourth.
<s>Soma</s> gave her to the <s>Gandharva</s>; the <s>Gandharva</s> gave her to <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: paśūṃś ca mahyaṃ putrāṃś cāgnir dadāty atho tvām
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> gives cattle and sons to me, and also you.

children.text: amūham asmi sā tvaṃ dyaur ahaṃ pṛthivī tvaṃ sāmāham ṛk tvaṃ tāv ehi saṃbhavāva saha reto dadhāvahai puṃse putrāya vettavai rāyaspoṣāya suprajāstvāya suvīryāya
children.translated_text: I am that one; you are she. I am heaven; you are earth. I am the <s>Sāman</s>; you are the <s>Ṛc</s>. Come, let us unite; together let us place the seed, to gain a male son, for wealth and nourishment, good offspring, and heroic strength.

children.text: imāṃ tvam indra mīḍhvaḥ suputrāṃ subhagāṃ kuru
children.translated_text: O bounteous <s>Indra</s>, make this woman blessed with good sons.

children.text: daśāsyāṃ putrān ādhehi patim ekādaśaṃ kuru
children.translated_text: Place ten sons in her; make her husband the eleventh.'
So the formulas run.

children.text: tāṃ yathāyatanam upaveśyāthāsyā añjalāv ājyenopastīrya lājān dvir āvapati
children.translated_text: Having seated her in the proper place, then having spread ghee in her joined palms, he pours parched grain into them twice.
'I pour in these parched grains, bringing prosperity for me.

children.text: tubhyaṃ ca saṃvananaṃ tad agnir anumanyatām ayam
children.translated_text: And let that winning of affection for you be approved by this <s>Agni</s>.'
So the formula runs.
Having sprinkled ghee over them,
'This woman speaks near, as she pours the parched grains into the fire:

children.text: dīrghāyur astu me patir edhantāṃ jñātayo mama
children.translated_text: May my husband be long-lived; may my kinsmen prosper.'
'Svāhā.'
So with her joined palms he offers the oblation.
With the verse 'With upward life,'
he raises her up.

children.text: viśvā uta tvayā vayaṃ dhārā udanyā iva
children.translated_text: 'By you may we, like streams with water,
pass beyond our enemies.'

children.text: iti pradakṣiṇam agniṃ parikramya tathaiva lājān āvapati ||
children.translated_text: Having thus circumambulated the fire clockwise, he pours in parched grains in the same way.
Having circumambulated a second time, he pours in parched grains in the same way.
Having circumambulated a third time, he offers the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> oblation.

children.text: atraike jayābhyātānān rāṣṭrabhṛta ity upajuhvati yathā purastāt ||
children.translated_text: At this point some offer additional oblations with the formulas beginning 'the victories,' 'the overtaken ones,' and 'the upholders of the realm,' as before.

children.text: tām apareṇāgniṃ prācīm udīcīṃ vā viṣṇukramān krāmayati ||
children.translated_text: West of the fire he makes her take the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-steps toward the east or toward the north.
Then he instructs her:

children.text: dakṣiṇena prakramya savyenānuprakrāma mā savyena dakṣiṇam atikrāmīḥ
children.translated_text: 'Starting with the right foot, follow with the left; do not step past the right with the left.'
So the formula runs.
'One step for nourishment; may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.'
'Two steps for strength; may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.'
'Three steps for the vow; may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.'
'Four steps for well-being; may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.'
'Five steps for cattle; may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.'
'Six steps for prosperity and increase; may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.'
'Seven steps for the seven hotṛ-priests; may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you.'
So the formula runs.
Having set down the seventh step, he murmurs:

children.text: sakhāyau saptapadāv abhūva sakhyaṃ te gameyaṃ sakhyāt te mā yoṣaṃ sakhyān me mā yoṣṭhāḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: 'We two have become friends, having taken seven steps. May I attain your friendship; may I not be separated from your friendship; may you not be separated from my friendship.' So the formula runs.

children.text: athāsyā dakṣiṇena pādena dakṣiṇaṃ pādam avakramya dakṣiṇena hastena dakṣiṇam aṃsam upary upary anvavamṛśya hṛdayadeśam abhimṛśati yathā purastāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, stepping with his right foot upon her right foot, and with his right hand touching her right shoulder repeatedly from above, he touches the region of the heart, as before.

children.text: prāṇānāṃ granthir asi sa mā visrasaḥ
children.translated_text: 'You are the knot of the breaths; do not loosen yourself from me.'
So he touches the region of the navel.

children.text: tām apareṇāgniṃ prācīm upaveśya purastāt pratyaṅ tiṣṭhann adbhiḥ prokṣati
children.translated_text: Having seated her east of the fire, facing east, he stands in front facing west and sprinkles her with water.
'For the waters are indeed bringers of bliss,'
with these three verses.
'Golden-colored, pure, purifying,'
with these four verses.
'The purifying one, winning heaven,'
and with this anuvāka.
Here they set seeds upon the fire.

children.text: tāṃ tataḥ pravāhayanti pra vā hārayanti ||
children.translated_text: Then they lead her forth, or have her led forth.
Having gathered this fire, they carry it after them.
It is to be maintained constantly.
If it has gone out, it is to be kindled by churning, or it is to be brought from the house of a learned <s>śrotriya</s>.
And if it has gone out, the wife or the husband must fast.
Having reached the house, he then instructs her:

children.text: dakṣiṇaṃ pādam agreti hara dehaliṃ mādhiṣṭhāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Put the right foot first; do not step on the threshold.'
So the formula runs.
Having deposited it in the eastern half of the hall, he lays the fire.

children.text: apareṇāgniṃ lohitam ānaḍuhaṃ carma prācīnagrīvam uttaralomāstṛṇāti ||
children.translated_text: West of the fire he spreads a red bull's hide, with its neck toward the east and its hair upward.
On it the two sit, facing east or facing north.
The wife sits behind the husband.

children.text: iha gāvo niṣīdantv ihāśvā iha pūruṣāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Here let the cows sit; here the horses; here the men.
Here also let <s>Pūṣan</s>, rich in a thousand gifts, sit.'
So the formula runs.
They remain under a vow of silence until the rising of the stars.

children.text: uditeṣu nakṣatreṣu prācīm udīcīṃ vā diśam upaniṣkramya
children.translated_text: When the stars have risen, having gone out toward the east or toward the north,
'O goddesses, the six broad ones,'
with this he reveres the directions.
'May we not be deprived of offspring,'
with this he reveres the stars.
'May we not fall under the power of the hater, O king <s>Soma</s>,'
with this he reveres the moon.

children.text: saptarṣayaḥ prathamāṃ kṛttikānām arundhatīṃ ye dhruvatāṃ ha ninyuḥ
children.translated_text: 'The Seven Seers, the first of the Kṛttikās, who indeed led <s>Arundhatī</s> to fixedness,
may this eighth one, bearing conjunction with the six Kṛttikās at their head, shine for us.'
Having revered the Seven Seers, he reveres <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: dhruvakṣitir dhruvayor nidhruvam asi dhruvata sthitam
children.translated_text: 'You are the fixed abode, fixed among the fixed, very fixed, standing firmly.

children.text: tvaṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ methy asi sa mā pāhi pṛtanyataḥ
children.translated_text: You are the peg of the stars; protect me from hostility.

children.text: namo brahmaṇe dhruvāyācyutāyāstu namo brahmaṇaḥ putrāya prajāpataye namo brahmaṇaḥ putrebhyo devebhyas trayastriṃśebhyo namo brahmaṇaḥ putrapautrebhyo 'ṅgirobhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Brahman</s>, the fixed, unfailing one; homage to <s>Prajāpati</s>, son of <s>Brahman</s>; homage to the gods, the thirty-three sons of <s>Brahman</s>; homage to the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, the sons and grandsons of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: yas tvā dhruvam acyutaṃ saputraṃ sapautraṃ brahma veda dhruvā asmin putrāḥ pautrā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Whoever knows you as fixed, unfailing <s>Brahman</s>, with sons and grandsons, in him sons and grandsons become fixed.

children.text: preṣyāntevāsino vasanaṃ kambalāni kaṃsaṃ hiraṇyaṃ striyo rājāno 'nnam abhayam āyuḥ kīrtir varco yaśo balaṃ brahmavarcasam annādyam ity etāni mayi sarvāṇi dhruvāṇy acyutāni santu ||
children.translated_text: Servants, pupils, clothing, blankets, bronze, gold, women, kings, food, fearlessness, life, fame, splendor, renown, strength, brahmanical brilliance, and food to eat: may all these be fixed and unfailing in me.'

children.text: dhruvaṃ tvā brahma veda dhruvo 'ham asmiṃl loke 'smiṃś ca janapade bhūyāsam
children.translated_text: '<s>Brahman</s> knows you as fixed; may I be fixed in this world and in this community.

children.text: acyutaṃ tvā brahma veda māham asmāl lokād asmāc ca janapadāc cyoṣi dviṣan me bhrātṛvyo 'smāl lokād asmāc ca janapadāc cyavatām
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> knows you as unfailing; may I not fall from this world and from this community. May the enemy, my rival, fall from this world and from this community.

children.text: aceṣṭaṃ tvā brahma veda māham asmāl lokād asmāc ca janapadāc ceṣṭiṣi dviṣan me bhrātṛvyo 'smāl lokād asmāc ca janapadāc ceṣṭatām
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> knows you as unmoving; may I not move away from this world and from this community. May the enemy, my rival, move away from this world and from this community.

children.text: avyathamānaṃ tvā brahma veda māham asmāl lokād asmāc ca janapadād vyathiṣi dviṣan me bhrātṛvyo 'smāl lokād asmāc ca janapadād vyathatām
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> knows you as unshaken; may I not be shaken from this world and from this community. May the enemy, my rival, be shaken from this world and from this community.

children.text: nabhyaṃ tvā sarvasya veda nabhyam aham asya janapadasya bhūyāsam
children.translated_text: He knows you as the navel of all; may I become the navel of this community.

children.text: madhyaṃ tvā sarvasya veda madhyam aham asya janapadasya bhūyāsam
children.translated_text: He knows you as the middle of all; may I become the middle of this community.

children.text: tantiṃ tvā sarvasya veda tantir aham asya janapadasya bhūyāsam
children.translated_text: He knows you as the strand of all; may I become the strand of this community.

children.text: methīṃ tvā sarvasya veda methy aham asya janapadasya bhūyāsam
children.translated_text: He knows you as the peg of all; may I become the peg of this community.

children.text: nābhiṃ tvā sarvasya veda nābhir aham asya janapadasya bhūyāsam
children.translated_text: He knows you as the hub of all; may I become the hub of this community.

children.text: yathā nābhiḥ prāṇānāṃ viṣūvān evam ahaṃ viṣūvān
children.translated_text: As the navel is the center of the breaths, so may I be the center.

children.text: ekaśataṃ taṃ pāpmānamṛcchatu yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmo bhūyāṃsi mām ekaśatāt puṇyāny āgacchantu
children.translated_text: May that evil, a hundred and onefold, reach the one who hates us and whom we hate; may merits more numerous than a hundred and one come to me.'
So the formula runs.

children.text: atra manojñena sambhāṣyāgāraṃ prāpyāthainām āgneyena sthālīpākena yājayati ||
children.translated_text: Here, after conversing pleasantly and reaching the house, he then has her perform the sacrifice with an āgneya pot-cooked offering.
The wife pounds the grain.
Having cooked it, sprinkled it with ghee, and taken it down, he offers to <s>Agni</s>, and offers to <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.
With that he serves a learned Brahmin.
To the one who is honored by her, he gives a bull.

children.text: nityam ata ūrdhvaṃ parvasv āgneyena sthālīpākena yajate ||
children.translated_text: From then on, at the parvan days, he regularly sacrifices with an āgneya pot-cooked offering.

children.text: nityaṃ sāyaṃ prātar vrīhibhir yavair vā hastenaite āhutī juhoti
children.translated_text: Every evening and morning he regularly offers these two oblations by hand with rice or barley:
'To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā.'
'To <s>Prajāpati</s>, svāhā.'
So it runs.
Some recite the preceding solar formula in the morning.

children.text: trirātram akṣārālavaṇāśināv adhaḥśāyināv alaṃkurvāṇau brahmacāriṇau vasataḥ ||
children.translated_text: For three nights the two, eating food without alkali and salt, sleeping on the ground, adorning themselves, and observing chastity, remain there.

children.text: caturthyām apararātre 'gnim upasamādhāya prāyaścittiparyantaṃ kṛtvā nava prāyaścittīr juhoti ||
children.translated_text: On the fourth, in the latter part of the night, having laid the fire and performed the rite as far as the expiatory formulas, he offers nine expiatory oblations.
Now then, the sīmantonnayana.

children.text: prathamagarbhāyāścaturthe māsyāpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye nakṣatregnimupasamādhāya vyāhṛtiparyantaṃ kṛtvā dhātā dadātu no rayim iti catasro dhātrīrjuhoti
children.translated_text: For a woman pregnant for the first time, in the fourth month, in the waxing fortnight, under an auspicious constellation, having laid the fire and performed the rite as far as the vyāhṛtis, he offers the four Dhātṛ oblations with 'May <s>Dhātṛ</s> give us wealth.'

children.text: imaṃ me varuṇa tattvā yāmi tvaṃ no agne sa tvaṃ no agne tvamagne ayāsi prajāpate yadasya karmaṇotyarīricam iti ca atraike jayābhyātānānrāṣṭrabhṛta ityupajuhvati yathā purastāt brāhmaṇānannena pariviṣya puṇyāhaṃ svastyayanamṛddhimiti vācayitvā snātāṃ prayatavastrāmalaṃkṛtāṃ brāhmaṇasaṃbhāṣāmapareṇāgniṃ maṇḍalāgāre prācīmupaveśya treṇyā śalalyā śalālugrapsamupasaṃgṛhya purastātpratyaṅtiṣṭhanvyāhṛtībhiḥ rākāmaham yāste rāke iti dvābhyāmūrdhvaṃ sīmantamunnīyābhimantrayate soma eva no rājetyāhurbrāhmaṇīḥ prajāḥ vivṛttacakrā āsīnāstīre tubhyaṃ gaṅge viśvā uta tvayā vayaṃ dhārā udanyā iva atigāhemahi dviṣaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: And with 'This for me, O <s>Varuṇa</s>,' 'That truth of you I approach,' 'You for us, O <s>Agni</s>,' 'So you for us, O <s>Agni</s>,' 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the expiation,' and 'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, whatever in this rite I have overdone,' some here add oblations with the formulas beginning 'the victories,' 'the overtaken ones,' and 'the upholders of the realm,' as before. Having entertained the Brahmins with food and made them pronounce 'auspicious day, welfare, prosperity,' he seats the woman, bathed, wearing clean garments, adorned, and addressed by the Brahmins, facing east west of the fire in a circular hut. Taking hold of a porcupine's quill, a cluster of śalālu, and a grape with a triple-pointed śalalī, he stands before her facing west; with the vyāhṛtis and with the two verses 'I invoke <s>Rākā</s>' and 'Whatever is yours, O <s>Rākā</s>,' he parts the hair upward and addresses her: 'They say that <s>Soma</s> alone is our king; the Brahmin women are offspring. Seated with wheels turned aside on the bank for you, O <s>Gaṅgā</s>, may we, by all of you, like streams with water, pass beyond our enemies.'
Now then, the puṃsavana.

children.text: tṛtīye māsyāpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre 'gnimupasamādhāya vyāhṛtiparyantaṃ kṛtvā dhātā dadātu no rayim iti catasro dhātrīrjuhoti imaṃ me varuṇa tattvā yāmi tvaṃ no 'gne sa tvaṃ no 'gne tvamagne ayāsi prajāpate yadasya karmaṇotparīricam iti ca atraike jayābhyātānānrāṣṭrabhṛta ityupajuhvati yathā purastāt brāhmaṇānannena pariviṣya puṇyāhaṃ svastyayanamṛddhimiti vācayitvā snātāṃ prayatavastrāmalaṃkṛtāṃ brāhmaṇasaṃbhāṣāmapareṇāgniṃ maṇḍalāgāre prācīmupaveśya vṛṣāsi iti tasyā dakṣiṇe pāṇau yavamādadhāti
children.translated_text: In the third month, in the waxing fortnight, under an auspicious constellation, having laid the fire and performed the rite as far as the vyāhṛtis, he offers the four Dhātṛ oblations with 'May <s>Dhātṛ</s> give us wealth,' and also with 'This for me, O <s>Varuṇa</s>,' 'That truth of you I approach,' 'You for us, O <s>Agni</s>,' 'So you for us, O <s>Agni</s>,' 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the expiation,' and 'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, whatever in this rite I have overdone.' Some here add oblations with the formulas beginning 'the victories,' 'the overtaken ones,' and 'the upholders of the realm,' as before. Having entertained the Brahmins with food and made them pronounce 'auspicious day, welfare, prosperity,' he seats the woman, bathed, wearing clean garments, adorned, and addressed by the Brahmins, facing east west of the fire in a circular hut. With 'You are a bull' he places barley in her right hand.

children.text: āṇḍau sthaḥ ityabhito yavaṃ sarṣapau dhānyamāṣau vā
children.translated_text: With 'You two are testicles,' he places two mustard seeds on either side of the barley, or two grains of rice and two beans.
With 'The dog has turned back,' he places a drop of curds; he makes her eat it.

children.text: ācāntāyā udaramabhimṛśati ābhiṣṭvāhaṃ daśabhirabhimṛśāmi daśamāsyāya sūtavai iti
children.translated_text: When she has sipped water, he touches her belly with 'With these ten I touch you for giving birth in the tenth month.'

children.text: nyagrodhaśṛṅgaṃ vā ghṛtena kośakārīṃ vā praiyaṅgaveṇa saṃyāvena yūpaśakalaṃ vottarapūrvasyābhiṣṭeragniṃ vā nirmanthya mūrumūlopadhānāyai dakṣiṇe nāsikāchidre praṇayet
children.translated_text: Or he should introduce a shoot of the banyan tree with ghee, or kośakārī with a gruel of praiyaṅgava, or a splinter of the sacrificial post from the north-eastern side, or fire produced by friction, into the right nostril, while she has the root of her thigh as a support.

children.text: yadi garbhaḥ sravedārdreṇāsyāḥ pāṇinā trirūrdhvaṃ nābherunmārṣṭi parāñcaṃ tvā nārvāñcaṃ tvaṣṭā badhnātu bandhane sa ṛtūnupaveśya daśa māso 'vīrahā iti
children.translated_text: If the embryo should be discharged, with his wet hand he wipes her three times upward above the navel: 'Neither away from you nor toward you; let <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> fasten it in the fastening. Having brought the seasons near, may it be ten months, not killing the hero.'

children.text: vijananakāle kṣipraprasavanam śirasta udakumbhaṃ nidhāya pattastūryantīmathāsyā udaramabhimṛśati ||
children.translated_text: At the time of delivery, for quick birth, having placed a water-pot at her head while she is straining with her feet spread, he then touches her belly.

children.text: yathaiva vāyuḥ pavate yathā samudra ejati evaṃ te garbha ejatu saha jarāyuṇāvasarpatu ityavāṅavamārṣṭi
children.translated_text: 'Just as the wind blows, just as the ocean stirs, so may your embryo stir and descend together with the afterbirth'; with this he wipes downward.

children.text: jāteśmani paraśuṃ nidhāyopariṣṭāddhiraṇyaṃ teṣūttarādhareṣūpariṣṭātkumāraṃ dhārayati aśmā bhava paraśurbhava hiraṇyamastṛtaṃ bhava vedo vai putranāmāsi jīva tvaṃ śaradaḥ śatam aṅgādaṅgātsaṃbhavasi hṛdayādadhijāyase ātmā vai putranāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śatamiti
children.translated_text: When the child is born, having placed an axe on a stone and gold above them, he holds the boy over those, above and below: 'Be a stone; be an axe; be unbroken gold. You are indeed called a son, the Veda; live a hundred autumns. From limb after limb you arise; from the heart you are born. You are indeed called a son, the self; live a hundred autumns.'

children.text: yadyaparā na patedañjalinodakamādāya mūrdhānamasyāvasiñcet tiladeva padyasva na māṃsamasi no dalam avapadyasva svapathāt iti
children.translated_text: If the afterbirth does not fall, having taken water in his joined hands, he should pour it over her head: 'Fall down like sesame. You are not flesh, nor a leaf. Fall down from your own path.'
They carry out the āupāsana fire; they carry in the sūtikā fire.
This one is precisely the fire to be heated.
No rite at all is performed in it except fumigation.

children.text: athainaṃ kaṇaiḥ sarṣapamiśrairuddhūpayati śaṇḍo marka upavīraḥ śāṇḍīkera ulūkhalaḥ cyavano naśyatāditaḥ svāhā ālikhanvilikhannanimiṣankiṃvadanta upaśrutiḥ svāhā aryamṇaḥ kumbhī śatruḥ pātrapāṇirnipuṇiḥ svāhā āntrīmukhaḥ sarṣapāruṇo naśyatāditaḥ svāhā keśinī śvalominī bajābojopakāśinī apeta naśyatāditaḥ svāhā kauberakā viśvavāso rakṣorājena preṣitāḥ grāmānsajātayo yantīpsantaḥ parijākṛtān svāhā etānhataitānbadhnītetyayaṃ brahmaṇo dūtastānagniḥ paryasarat tānindrastānbṛhaspatistānahaṃ veda brāhmaṇaḥ pramṛśataḥ kūṭadantānvikeśālla￢mbastanān svāhā naktaṃcāriṇa uraspeśāñchūlahastānkapālapān svāhā pūrva eṣām pitetyuccaiḥśrāvyakarṇakaḥ mātā jaghanyā gachanti grāme vikhuramicchantī svāhā naktaṃcāriṇī svasā sandhinā prekṣate kulam yā svapatsu jāgarti yasyai vijātāyāṃ manaḥ svāhā tāsāṃ tvaṃ kṛṣṇavartmane klomānaṃ hṛdayaṃ yakṛt agneyakṣīṇi nirdaha svāhā iti pratimantramaṅgāreṣvāvapati
children.translated_text: Then he fumigates him with grains mixed with mustard: '<s>Śaṇḍa</s>, <s>Marka</s>, <s>Upavīra</s>, <s>Śāṇḍīkera</s>, <s>Ulūkhala</s>, <s>Cyavana</s>, perish from here, svāhā. Scratching, scraping, unblinking, saying “what?”, overhearing, svāhā. The pot of <s>Aryaman</s>, the enemy, the one with a vessel in his hand, the clever one, svāhā. Intestine-mouthed, mustard-red, perish from here, svāhā. Hairy one, dog-haired one, revealing bajā and boja, depart, perish from here, svāhā. The <s>Kauberaka</s>s, sent by <s>Viśvavasu</s> with the king of the <s>Rakṣas</s>es, go to villages and kinsmen, desiring those who have been driven around, svāhā. Strike these, bind these: this is the messenger of <s>Brahman</s>. <s>Agni</s> has gone around them, <s>Indra</s> has gone around them, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> has gone around them. I, a Brahmin, know them as they touch: with false teeth, dishevelled hair, and pendulous breasts, svāhā. Night-roamers, breast-spotted, holding spears, drinking from skulls, svāhā. Their father is in front, the high-eared one with audible ears; their mother, the hindmost, goes about in the village, seeking confusion, svāhā. Their sister, a night-roamer, looks at the household through the joints; she who wakes among those who sleep, whose mind is on the woman who has given birth, svāhā. O you of the black path, burn out their lungs, heart, liver, and fiery eyes, svāhā.' Thus, with each formula, he throws it upon the embers.

children.text: tataḥ pāṇī prakṣālya bhūmimālabhate yatte susīme hṛdayaṃ divi candramasi śritam tasyāmṛtatvasya no dhehi māhaṃ pautramaghaṃ rudam veda te bhūmi hṛdayaṃ divi candramasi śritam tathāmṛtatvasyeśāno māhaṃ pautramaghaṃ rudamiti iti
children.translated_text: Then, having washed his hands, he touches the earth: 'Whatever heart of yours, O well-bounded one, rests in heaven, in the moon, place us in the immortality belonging to it; may I not weep for misfortune to a grandson. I know your heart, O earth, resting in heaven, in the moon. As lord of immortality, may I not weep for misfortune to a grandson.' Thus it runs.

children.text: athāto medhājananam darbheṇa hiraṇyaṃ prabadhya tadantardhāyopariṣṭātprāñcaṃ kumāraṃ dhāryamāṇaṃ ghṛtaṃ prāśayati bhūrṛcastvayi juhomi svāhā bhuvo yajūṃṣi tvayi juhomi svāhā suvaḥ sāmāni tvayi juhomi svāhā bhūrbhuvaḥ suvaratharvāṅgirasastvayi juhomi svāhā iti
children.translated_text: Now, next, the generation of intelligence. Having tied gold to a blade of darbha grass, placed it within it, and set the boy, held facing east, above it, he makes him eat ghee: '<s>Bhūḥ</s>, I pour the <s>Ṛc</s> verses into you, svāhā. <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, I pour the <s>Yajus</s> formulas into you, svāhā. <s>Suvaḥ</s>, I pour the <s>Sāman</s> chants into you, svāhā. <s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ</s>, I pour the <s>Atharvāṅgiras</s> texts into you, svāhā.'

children.text: athainamuṣṇaśītābhiradbhiḥ snāpayati kṣetriyai tvā nirṛtyai tvā druho muñcāmi varuṇasya pāśāt anāgasaṃ brahmaṇe tvā karomi śive te dyāvāpṛthivī ubhe ime śaṃ te agniḥ sahādbhirastu śaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī sahauṣadhībhiḥ śamantarikṣaṃ saha vātena te śaṃ te catasraḥ pradiśo bhavantu sūryamṛtaṃ tamaso grāhyā yaddevā amuñcannasṛjanvyenasaḥ evamahamimaṃ kṣetriyājjāmiśaṃsāddruho muñcāmi varuṇasya pāśāt iti
children.translated_text: Then he bathes him with warm and cold waters: 'From disease of the field, from <s>Nirṛti</s>, from malice, I release you from the noose of <s>Varuṇa</s>. Free from guilt I make you over to <s>Brahman</s>. May these two, heaven and earth, be auspicious for you. May <s>Agni</s> together with the waters be welfare for you. May heaven and earth together with the herbs be welfare for you. May the midspace together with the wind be welfare for you. May the four directions be welfare for you. The immortal sun from darkness, from seizure: as the gods released and freed him from guilt, so I release this one from disease of the field, from accusation by kin, from malice, and from the noose of <s>Varuṇa</s>.'
Then he places him in the mother's lap.

children.text: yā daivīścatasraḥ pradiśo vātapatnīrabhi sūryo vicaṣṭe tāsāṃ tvā jarasa ādadhāmi pra yakṣma etu nirṛtiṃ parācaiḥ iti
children.translated_text: 'The four divine directions, wives of the wind, over which the sun looks abroad: into them I place you for old age. Let consumption go away toward <s>Nirṛti</s>, turned away.'

children.text: ādhāyābhimantrayate mā te putraṃ rakṣo hiṃsīnmā dhenuratisāriṇī priyā dhanasya bhūyā edhamānā sve vaśe iti
children.translated_text: Having placed him there, he addresses him: 'Let no <s>Rakṣas</s> injure your son; let no over-running cow do so. May you be dear to wealth, growing in your own power.'

children.text: prakṣālya dakṣiṇaṃ stanamādhāpayati ayaṃ kumāro jarāṃ dhayatu sarvamāyuretu tasmai stanaṃ prapyāyasvāyuḥ kīrtirvarco yaśo balam iti
children.translated_text: Having washed the right breast, he makes her give it to him: 'May this boy suck old age; may he reach his full lifetime. For him, O breast, swell with life, fame, brilliance, renown, and strength.'
The same with the left breast.

children.text: nāmayati na rudati yatra vayaṃ vadāmo yatra vābhimṛśāmasi ityubhāvabhimṛśyāthāsyai śirasta udakumbhamapihitaṃ nidadhāti āpo gṛheṣu jāgrata yathā deveṣu jāgratha evamasyai suputrāyai jāgrata iti
children.translated_text: He bends him down; he does not cry where we speak, or where we touch. Having touched them both, he then places at her head a covered water-pot: 'Waters, keep watch in the houses, as you keep watch among the gods; so keep watch over this woman with good sons.'
On the twelfth day the mother and son, bathed,
make a clean dwelling.
They carry out the sūtikā fire and carry in the āupāsana fire.

children.text: tamagnimupasamādhāya vyāhṛtiparyantaṃ kṛtvā dhātā dadātu no rayim iti dvādaśāhutīrjuhoti trayodaśetyekeṣām
children.translated_text: Having laid that fire and performed the rite as far as the vyāhṛtis, he offers twelve oblations with 'May <s>Dhātṛ</s> give us wealth'; according to some, thirteen.

children.text: imaṃ me varuṇa tattvā yāmi tvaṃ no agne sa tvaṃ no agne tvamagne ayāsi prajāpate yadasya karmaṇotyarīricam iti ca atraike jayābhyātānānrāṣṭrabhṛta ityupajuhvati yathā purastāt brāhmaṇānannena pariviṣya puṇyāhaṃ svastyayanamṛddhimiti vācayitvā putrasya nāma dadhyāddvyakṣaraṃ caturakṣaraṃ vā ghoṣavadādyantarantasthaṃ dīrghābhiniṣṭhānāntaṃ yatra vā svityupasargaḥ syāt taddhi pratiṣṭhitamiti vijñāyate
children.translated_text: With 'This for me, O <s>Varuṇa</s>,' 'That truth of yours I approach,' 'You for us, O <s>Agni</s>,' 'So you for us, O <s>Agni</s>,' 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the expiation,' and 'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, whatever in this rite I have overdone,' some here add oblations with the formulas beginning 'the victories,' 'the overtaken ones,' and 'the upholders of the realm,' as before. Having entertained the Brahmins with food and made them pronounce 'auspicious day, welfare, prosperity,' he should give the son a name of two syllables or four syllables, with a voiced sound at the beginning, an internal semivowel at the end, and ending in a long vowel, or one in which the prefix 'su' occurs; for that, it is known, is well established.

children.text: pitā mātetyagrebhivyāhareyātām vijñāyate ca mama nāma prathamaṃ jātaveda iti
children.translated_text: The father and mother should pronounce it first. And it is known: 'My name first, O <s>Jātavedas</s>.'

children.text: dve nāmanī kuryāt vijñāyate ca tasmāddvināmā brāhmaṇordhuka iti
children.translated_text: He should make two names. And it is known: 'Therefore a Brahmin has two names, O <s>Ūrdhuka</s>.'
The second should be the nakṣatra-name; one of the two should be secret.
They should address him by either one.
It is known that a soma-sacrificer should make a third name.

children.text: pravāsādetyāgataṃ vā putramabhimṛśati somasya tvā dyumnenābhimṛśāmyagnestejasā sūryasya varcasā iti
children.translated_text: He touches a son who has come back from being abroad, or who has arrived: 'With the glory of <s>Soma</s> I touch you, with the fiery power of <s>Agni</s>, with the brilliance of the sun.'

children.text: paśūnāṃ tvā huṃkāreṇābhijighrāmyasāvāyuṣe varcase hum iti mūrdhnyabhijighrya
children.translated_text: 'With the bellowing of cattle I smell you, so-and-so, for life and brilliance, hum.' Having smelled him on the head,

children.text: athāsya dakṣiṇena hastena dakṣiṇaṃ hastaṃ sāṅguṣṭhaṃ gṛhṇāti agnirāyuṣmān iti pañcabhiḥ paryāyaiḥ
children.translated_text: then with his right hand he takes the son's right hand, including the thumb, with the five turns beginning 'Agni is long-lived.'

children.text: āyuṣṭe viśvato dadhat iti dakṣiṇe karṇe japati yathā purastāt ||
children.translated_text: With 'placing life for you on every side,' he murmurs into the right ear, as before.
Then, in the sixth month, the first feeding of solid food.

children.text: āpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye nakṣatregnimupasamādhāya vyāhṛtiparyantaṃ kṛtvā juhoti imaṃ me varuṇa tattvā yāmi tvaṃ no agne sa tvaṃ no agne tvamagne ayāsi prajāpate yadasya karmaṇotyarīricam iti ca atraike yajābhyātānānrāṣṭrabhṛta ityupajuhvati yathā purastāt brāhmaṇānannena pariviṣya puṇyāhaṃ svastyayanamṛddhimiti vācayitvāthainaṃ dadhi madhu ghṛtamiti trivṛtprāśayati bhūstvayi dadhāmi bhuvastvayi dadhāmi suvastvayi dadhāmi iti
children.translated_text: In the waxing fortnight, under an auspicious constellation, having laid the fire and performed the rite up to the vyāhṛtis, he offers with 'This for me, O <s>Varuṇa</s>,' 'That truth of you I approach,' 'You for us, O <s>Agni</s>,' 'So you for us, O <s>Agni</s>,' 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the expiation,' and 'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, whatever in this rite I have overdone.' Some here add oblations with the formulas beginning 'the victories,' 'the overtaken ones,' and 'the upholders of the realm,' as before. Having entertained the Brahmins with food and made them pronounce 'auspicious day, welfare, prosperity,' he then makes him taste the threefold mixture, curds, honey, and ghee, with 'I place bhūḥ in you; I place bhuvaḥ in you; I place suvaḥ in you.'

children.text: athainamannaṃ prāśayati apāṃ tvauṣadhīnāṃ rasaṃ prāśayāmi śivāsta āpa oṣadhayaḥ santvanamīvāsta āpa oṣadhayo bhavantu iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he makes him taste food: 'I make you taste the sap of the waters and plants. May the waters and plants be auspicious for you; may the waters and plants be free from sickness for you.'
In the third year, the tonsure rite.

children.text: āpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye nakṣatregnimupasamādhāya vyāhṛtiparyantaṃ kṛtvā juhoti imaṃ me varuṇa tattvā yāmi tvaṃ no agne sa tvaṃ no agne tvamagne ayāsi prajāpate yadasya karmaṇotyarīricam iti ca atraike jayābhyātānānrāṣṭrabhṛta ityupajuhvati yathā purastāt brāhmaṇānannena pariviṣya puṇyāhaṃ svastyayanamṛddhimiti vācayitvāpareṇāgniṃ prāṅmukhaḥ kumāra upaviśati
children.translated_text: In the waxing fortnight, under an auspicious constellation, having laid the fire and performed the rite up to the vyāhṛtis, he offers with 'This for me, O <s>Varuṇa</s>,' 'That truth of you I approach,' 'You for us, O <s>Agni</s>,' 'So you for us, O <s>Agni</s>,' 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the expiation,' and 'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, whatever in this rite I have overdone.' Some here add oblations with the formulas beginning 'the victories,' 'the overtaken ones,' and 'the upholders of the realm,' as before. Having entertained the Brahmins with food and made them pronounce 'auspicious day, welfare, prosperity,' the boy sits west of the fire, facing east.

children.text: uttarato mātā brahmacārī vānaḍuhaṃ śakṛtpiṇḍaṃ dhārayati
children.translated_text: To the north, the mother or a brahmacārin holds a lump of bull's dung.
With it he receives the boy's hair.
Then he mixes hot and cold waters.

children.text: śītāsūṣṇā ānīya āpa undantu jīvase iti dakṣiṇaṃ godānamunatti
children.translated_text: Having brought hot water into the cold, he moistens the right godāna lock with 'May the waters moisten you for life.'
With 'O plant, protect him,' he places a plant with its tip upward between them.
With 'O razor, do not injure him,' he applies the razor.
With 'These are divine razors; shave them,' he shaves.

children.text: evamitarānpradakṣiṇam yenāvapatsavitā kṣureṇa somasya rājño varuṇasya vidvān tena brahmāṇo vapatedamasya ūrjemaṃ rayyā varcasā saṃsṛjātha iti paścāt yena pūṣā bṛhaspateragnerindrasya cāyuṣevapat tena tehaṃ vapāmyasau ityuttarataḥ yathā jyoksumanā asat jyokca sūryaṃ dṛśe iti purastāt
children.translated_text: In the same way he shaves the others clockwise: behind, with 'With the razor with which <s>Savitṛ</s>, knowing, shaved <s>Soma</s> the king and <s>Varuṇa</s>, with that let the Brahmins shave this one; join him with strength, wealth, and brilliance'; to the north, with 'With that with which <s>Pūṣan</s> shaved <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and <s>Indra</s> for long life, with that I shave you, so-and-so'; in front, with 'So that he may long be well-minded and long see the sun.'

children.text: uptvā yathocitaṃ cūḍāḥ kārayati yatharṣi vā
children.translated_text: After shaving, he has the crests made in the proper way, or according to the seer tradition.

children.text: saṃyamya keśān yatra pūṣā bṛhaspatiḥ savitā somo agniḥ tebhyo nidhānaṃ bahudhā vyaicchannantarā dyāvāpṛthavī apaḥ suvaḥ iti goṣṭha udumbare darbhastambe vā nikhanati yosya rātirbhavati
children.translated_text: Having gathered the hair together, he buries it in a cow-pen, in an udumbara tree, or in a clump of darbha, with 'Where <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and <s>Agni</s> sought many places of deposit between heaven and earth, the waters, and heaven'; this becomes his gift.
According to his faith, he gives something to a Brahmin.
He gives rice cooked with ghee to the barber.
In the same prescribed way, in the sixteenth year, is the godāna rite.
He has the hair shaved, leaving the topknot.
According to some, he omits the topknot formulas.
Or it may be the fire-godāna.
He gives a cow to the teacher.
Now then, the expiation for śvagraha, seizure by a dog.

children.text: samupasṛte yajñopavītyācāntonāprītena śarāveṇodakamāhṛtya sabhāyāṃ madhyedhidevanamuddhatyāvokṣyākṣānnyupya vyūhya samūhya prathayitvopariṣṭātsabhāyāṃ vyūhya tṛṇāni tena kumāramabhyāhṛtyākṣeṣūttānaṃ nipātya dadhnā lavaṇodakamiśreṇābhyukṣati āghnanti kaṃsaṃ dakṣiṇataḥ kurkuraḥ sukurkuraḥ kurkuro nīlabandhanaḥ aulava ittamupāhvayatārjima chambalaḥ athorāma ulumbaraḥ sārameyo ha dhāvati samudramiva cākaśadbibhranniṣkaṃ ca rukmaṃ ca śunāmagraṃ suvīriṇaḥ suvīriṇaḥ sṛja sṛja ekavrātya sṛja śunaka sṛja chat ṭekaśca sasaramaṭaṅkaśca tūlaśca vitūlaścārjunaśca lohitaśca utsṛja tvaṃ śitimra tvaṃ piśaṃka rohitaḥ amī ye ke sarasyakā avadhāvati tṛtīyasyāmito divi chadapehi sīsarama sārameya namaste astu sīsara dūtyā ha nāma vo mātā maṇḍākako ha vaḥ pitā chadapehi sīsarama sārameya namaste astu sīsara dulā ha nāma vo mātā maṇḍākako ha vaḥ pitā chadapehi sisarama sārameya namaste astu sīsara samaśvā vṛṣaṇaḥ pado na sīsaridataḥ chadapehi sīsarama sārameya namaste astu sīsara saṃtakṣā hanti cakriṇo na sīsaridataḥ chadapehi sīsarama sārameya namaste astu sīsara iti
children.translated_text: When it has approached, wearing the sacred thread and having sipped water, he brings water in an unbaked bowl, clears the gaming place in the middle of the assembly hall, sprinkles it, casts down the dice, spreads them out, gathers them, lays them flat, again spreads them out above in the assembly hall, and spreads grass there. Having brought the boy there with that, he lays him face-up on the dice and sprinkles him with curds mixed with salt water. They strike a bronze vessel to the south: '<s>Kurkura</s>, <s>Sukurkura</s>, <s>Kurkura</s> of the blue bond, <s>Aulava</s> called thus to <s>Ṛjima</s> and <s>Chambala</s>. Then <s>Rāma Ulumbara</s>; the <s>Sārameya</s> runs, appearing like the ocean, bearing a niṣka and a gold ornament, foremost of dogs, rich in heroes. Rich in heroes, release, release; O sole vrātya, release; O dog, release. Chatt, <s>Ṭeka</s>, <s>Sasaramaṭaṅka</s>, <s>Tūla</s>, <s>Vitūla</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, and <s>Lohita</s>; release. You are <s>Śitimra</s>; you are tawny, reddish. Those, whoever are in the lake, run away from here in the third heaven. Go away, <s>Sīsarama Sārameya</s>; homage to you, <s>Sīsara</s>. <s>Dūtyā</s> is the name of your mother; <s>Maṇḍākaka</s> is your father. Go away, <s>Sīsarama Sārameya</s>; homage to you, <s>Sīsara</s>. <s>Dulā</s> is the name of your mother; <s>Maṇḍākaka</s> is your father. Go away, <s>Sisarama Sārameya</s>; homage to you, <s>Sīsara</s>. The horses together, the bulls, the feet, do not hiss from here. Go away, <s>Sīsarama Sārameya</s>; homage to you, <s>Sīsara</s>. The carpenter strikes; the wheel-bearers do not hiss from here. Go away, <s>Sīsarama Sārameya</s>; homage to you, <s>Sīsara</s>.'
Then he says, 'Choose a boon.'
'I choose the boy himself as the boon,' he says.

children.text: evaṃ samupasṛte triranhaḥ prātarmadhyaṃdine sāyaṃ ca kuryādyadi cāgataḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: When it has thus approached, he should do this three times a day, in the morning, at midday, and in the evening, if it has come.
Now then, the śūlagava rite.

children.text: āpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye nakṣatregnimupasamādhāya saṃparistīrya payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvābhighāryodvāsyāpareṇāgniṃ dve kuṭī kṛtvā dakṣiṇasyāṃ śūlagavamāvāhayati ā tvā vahantu harayaḥ sacetasaḥ śvetairaśvaiḥ saha ketumadbhiḥ vātājirairbalavadbhirmanojavairāyāhi śīdhraṃ mama havyāya śarvom iti
children.translated_text: In the waxing fortnight, under an auspicious constellation, having laid the fire, strewn it round, cooked a mess of rice in milk, sprinkled it with ghee, and taken it from the fire, he makes two huts west of the fire. In the southern one he invokes <s>Śūlagava</s>: 'May the bay steeds bring you, of one mind, together with white horses bearing banners, swift as the wind, strong, quick as thought. Come quickly for my oblation, O <s>Śarva</s>.'
In the northern one he invokes <s>Mīḍhuṣī</s>.
In the middle, <s>Jayanta</s>.

children.text: yathoḍhumudakāni pradāyopastīrṇābhighāritāṃstrīnodanānkalpayitvā yathoḍhamevopasparśayati upaspṛśatu mīḍhvānmīḍhuṣe svāhā upaspṛśatu mīḍhuṣī mīḍhuṣyai svāhā jayanta upaspṛśatu jayantāya svāhā iti
children.translated_text: Having given water according to the way they were brought, and having prepared three portions of cooked rice that have been spread under and sprinkled with ghee, he makes them touch water in the same order: 'Let <s>Mīḍhvān</s> touch water; svāhā to <s>Mīḍhuṣ</s>. Let <s>Mīḍhuṣī</s> touch water; svāhā to <s>Mīḍhuṣī</s>. Let <s>Jayanta</s> touch water; svāhā to <s>Jayanta</s>.'

children.text: vyāhṛtiparyantaṃ kṛtvaudanānabhyāhṛtya juhoti bhavāya devāya svāhā rudrāya devāya svāhā śarvāya devāya svāhā īśānāya devāya svāhā paśupataye devāya svāhā ugrāya devāya svāhā bhīmāya devāya svāhā mahate devāya svāhā iti
children.translated_text: Having performed the rite up to the vyāhṛtis, he takes portions from the rice messes and offers: 'Svāhā to the god <s>Bhava</s>; svāhā to the god <s>Rudra</s>; svāhā to the god <s>Śarva</s>; svāhā to the god <s>Īśāna</s>; svāhā to the god <s>Paśupati</s>; svāhā to the god <s>Ugra</s>; svāhā to the god <s>Bhīma</s>; svāhā to the great god.'

children.text: atha patnyodanasya patnyai juhoti bhavasya devasya patnyai svāhā rudrasya devasya patnyai svāhā śarvasya devasya patnyai svāhā īśānasya devasya patnyai svāhā paśupaterdevasya patnyai svāhā ugrasya devasya patnyai svāhā bhīmasya devasya patnyai svāhā mahato devasya patnyai svāhā iti
children.translated_text: Then, from the wife's rice, he offers to the wife: 'Svāhā to the wife of the god <s>Bhava</s>; svāhā to the wife of the god <s>Rudra</s>; svāhā to the wife of the god <s>Śarva</s>; svāhā to the wife of the god <s>Īśāna</s>; svāhā to the wife of the god <s>Paśupati</s>; svāhā to the wife of the god <s>Ugra</s>; svāhā to the wife of the god <s>Bhīma</s>; svāhā to the wife of the great god.'

children.text: atha madhyamaudanasya juhoti jayantāya svāhā jayantāya svāhā iti
children.translated_text: Then, from the middle rice, he offers: 'Svāhā to <s>Jayanta</s>; svāhā to <s>Jayanta</s>.'

children.text: atha savahhbhya odanebhyaḥ samavadāya sauviṣṭakṛtīṃ juhoti agnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā iti
children.translated_text: Then, having taken portions together from all the rice messes, he offers the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> oblation: 'Svāhā to <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>.'

children.text: abhita etamagniṃ gā sthāpayanti yathā hūyamānasya gandhamājighreyuḥ
children.translated_text: They set cows around this fire so that they may smell the scent of the offering as it is being made.

children.text: svasti naḥ pūrṇamukhaṃ parikrāmantu iti sarvataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ parikramya namaste rudra manyave ityetairanuvākairupatiṣṭhate prathamottamābhyāṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: After going all the way around clockwise with 'May those with full mouths circle us for welfare,' he worships with the anuvākas beginning 'Homage to your wrath, O <s>Rudra</s>,' or with the first and last of them.
Now then, in the same way, there is the <s>Bauḍhya</s> observance.

children.text: gṛhapopaspṛśa gṛhapāya svāhā gṛhapyupaspṛśa gṛhapyai svāhā dvārapopaspṛśa dvārapāya svāhā dvārapyupaspṛśa dvārapyai svāhā iti catvāri palāśāni dadāti ghoṣiṇa upaspṛśata ghoṣibhyaḥ svāhā niṣaṅgiṇa upaspṛśata niṣaṅgibhyaḥ svāhā anvāsāriṇa upaspṛśatānvāsāribhyaḥ svāhā prayunvanta upaspṛśata prayunvadbhyaḥ svāhā vicinvanta upaspṛśata vicinvadbhyaḥ svāhā samaśnanta upaspṛśata samaśnadbhyaḥ svāhā iti
children.translated_text: 'Householder, touch water; svāhā to the householder. Housewife, touch water; svāhā to the housewife. Doorkeeper, touch water; svāhā to the doorkeeper. Doorwoman, touch water; svāhā to the doorwoman.' Thus he gives four palāśa leaves. 'You noisy ones, touch water; svāhā to the noisy ones. You quiver-bearers, touch water; svāhā to the quiver-bearers. You followers, touch water; svāhā to the followers. You who set in motion, touch water; svāhā to those who set in motion. You who search out, touch water; svāhā to those who search out. You who eat together, touch water; svāhā to those who eat together.'

children.text: daśāthāparāṇi devasenā upaspṛśata devasenābhyaḥ svāhā iti
children.translated_text: Then he gives ten further ones: 'Armies of the gods, touch water; svāhā to the armies of the gods.'

children.text: daśaivāthāparāṇi yā ākhyātā devasenā yāścānākhyātā upaspṛśata tābhyaḥ svāhā iti
children.translated_text: And again ten further ones: 'Those armies of the gods that are named and those that are unnamed, touch water; svāhā to them.'

children.text: atha parṇapuṭaṃ kṛtvā tasminnupastīrṇābhighāritamodanapiṇḍamavadāya paro gavyūtiṃ gatvā vṛkṣa āsajati niṣaṅgiṇa upaspṛśata niṣaṅgibhyaḥ svāhā iti
children.translated_text: Then, having made a leaf packet, he takes into it a lump of cooked rice that has been spread under and sprinkled with ghee, goes more than a gavyūti away, and hangs it on a tree: 'You quiver-bearers, touch water; svāhā to the quiver-bearers.'

children.text: athopatiṣṭhate namo niṣaṅgiṇa iṣudhimate taskarāṇāṃ pataye iti
children.translated_text: Then he worships: 'Homage to the quiver-bearer, armed with arrows, lord of thieves.'

children.text: atha cāndanasurodakākṣatākṣatagomayadūrvāstambodumbarapalāśaśamīvaikaṅkatāśvatthena govāleneti gāḥ prokṣati vṛṣāṇamevāgre śivo bhava śivo bhava ityatha śivo haiva bhavati
children.translated_text: Then with sandal-water, unbroken grains, unbroken cow-dung, dūrvā grass, bunches of udumbara, palāśa, śamī, vaikaṅkata, and aśvattha, and with a cow-tail, he sprinkles the cows, the bull first, saying, 'Be auspicious, be auspicious.' Then it indeed becomes auspicious.

children.text: athainaṃ kṣaitrapatyaṃ payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvābhighāryodvāsya gavāṃ mārgenagnau kṣetrasya patiṃ yajati
children.translated_text: Then, for this <s>Kṣetrapati</s> rite, having cooked a mess of rice in milk, sprinkled it with ghee, and removed it from the fire, he sacrifices to the lord of the field in the fire on the path of the cows.

children.text: caturṣu saptasu vā palāśeṣu taṃ tathaivāvāhayati yathā śūlagavam
children.translated_text: On four or seven palāśa leaves he invokes him in just the same way as <s>Śūlagava</s>.
At the sacrifice, the cooked offering is the deity.

children.text: athopatiṣṭhatae kṣetrasya patinā vayaṃ kṣetrasya pate iti
children.translated_text: Then he worships with 'With the lord of the field may we,' and 'O lord of the field.'

children.text: athaitasya kṣaitrapatyasya ye sanābhayo bhavanti te prāśnanti yathaivaiṣāṃ kuladharmo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Then the kinsmen of this <s>Kṣetrapati</s> offering eat it, just as their family custom may be.
On the new-moon day, in the afternoon, or monthly, on the days of the dark fortnight when the wind is favorable,

children.text: pitṛbhyonnaṃ saṃskṛtya dakṣiṇāgrāndarbhānāsanāni kalpayitvā brāhmaṇāñchucīnmantravataḥ samaṅgānayuja āmantrayate yonigotramantrāsaṃbandhān
children.translated_text: having prepared food for the ancestors, having arranged seats of darbha grass with their tips to the south, he invites pure Brahmins, versed in the mantras, whole-limbed, and in an odd number, who are connected by womb, lineage, mantra, and relationship.
He should not feed anyone who is motivated by profit.

children.text: agnimupasamādhāya dakṣiṇāprāgagrairdarbhaiḥ paristīryaikapavitrāntarhitāyāmājyasthālyāmājyaṃ saṃskṛtya prasavyaṃ pariṣicyaudumbaramidhmamabhyādhāyaudumbaryā darvyā juhoti
children.translated_text: Having laid the fire, strewn it round with darbha grass whose tips point south-east, prepared ghee in a ghee-vessel separated by a single purifier, sprinkled it counterclockwise, and put on udumbara fuel, he offers with an udumbara ladle.

children.text: ājyabhāgāntaṃ kṛtvā prācīnāvītī pit￣nāvāhayati āyāta pitaraḥ somyā gambhīraiḥ pathibhiḥ pūrvyaiḥ prajāmasmabhyaṃ dadato rayiṃ ca dīrghāyutvaṃ ca śataśāradaṃ ca iti
children.translated_text: Having performed the rite up to the ājyabhāga offerings, wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, he invokes the fathers: 'Come here, O Soma-drinking fathers, by the ancient deep paths, giving us offspring and wealth, long life, and a hundred autumns.'

children.text: etāmeva diśamabhyapaḥ prasiñcati āpo devīḥ prahiṇutāgnimetaṃ yajñaṃ pitaro no juṣantām māsīmāmūrjamuta ye bhajante te no rayiṃ sarvavīraṃ niyacchantu iti
children.translated_text: In this same direction he pours water: 'Divine waters, send forth this fire. May our fathers enjoy the sacrifice. Those who partake of this monthly nourishment, let them assign to us wealth with all heroes.'

children.text: yajñopavītī vyāhṛtiparyantaṃ kṛtvā prācīnāvītī juhoti somāya pitṛmate svadhā namaḥ yamāyāṅgirasvate pitṛmate svadhā namaḥ yāḥ prācīḥ saṃbhavantyāpa uttarataśca yā adbhirviśvasya bhuvanasya dhartrībhirantaranyaṃ piturdadhe svadhā namaḥ antardadhe parvatairantarmahyā pṛthivyā divā digbhiranantābhirūtibhirantaranyaṃ pitāmahāddadhe svadhā namaḥ antardadha ṛtubhirahorātraiḥ susandhibhirardhamāsaiśca māsaiścāntaranyaṃ prapitāmahāddadhe svadhā namaḥ iti atha nāmadheyairjuhoti amuṣmai svadhā namaḥ amuṣmai svadhā namaḥ iti yanme mātā pralulobha caratyananuvratā tanme retaḥ pitā vṛṅktāmābhuranyopapadyatām svadhā namaḥ iti evaṃ dvitīyāṃ tathā tṛtīyām yanme pitāmahī yanme prapitāmahī iti mantraṃ saṃnamati ||
children.translated_text: Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, after performing the rite up to the vyāhṛtis, he offers with the sacred thread over the right shoulder: 'To <s>Soma</s>, accompanied by the fathers, svadhā, homage. To <s>Yama Aṅgirasvat</s>, accompanied by the fathers, svadhā, homage. The waters that come together in the east, and those in the north, with the waters that are the supports of all existence, I set another apart from my father; svadhā, homage. I set him apart by mountains, within the great earth, by heaven, by the quarters, and by endless protections; I set another apart from my grandfather; svadhā, homage. I set him apart by the seasons, by days and nights with their good junctions, by half-months and by months; I set another apart from my great-grandfather; svadhā, homage.' Then he offers with their names: 'To so-and-so, svadhā, homage. To so-and-so, svadhā, homage.' 'Whatever my mother, going astray and not following her vow, has desired, may my father take that seed from me; may another, not fit for it, attain it; svadhā, homage.' In the same way he offers a second and likewise a third, adapting the mantra with 'Whatever my grandmother,' and 'Whatever my great-grandmother.'

children.text: ye ceha pitaro ye ca neha yāṃśca vidma yā￢ u ca na pravidma agne tānvettha yadi te jātavedastayā prattaṃ svadhayā madantu svadhā namaḥ yadvaḥ kravyādaṅgamadahallokānayaṃ praṇayañjātavedāḥ tadvohaṃ punarāveśayāmyariṣṭāḥ sarvairaṅgaiḥ saṃbhavata pitaraḥ svadhā namaḥ vahājyaṃ jātavedaḥ pitṛbhyo yatraitānvettha nihitānparāke ājyasya kūlyā upa tānkṣarantu satyā eṣāmāśiṣaḥ santu kāmaiḥ svadhā namaḥ iti evaṃ dvitīyāṃ tathā tṛtīyām pitāmahebhyaḥ prapitāmahebhyaḥ iti mantraṃ saṃnamati
children.translated_text: 'Those fathers who are here and those who are not here, those whom we know and those whom we do not know, O <s>Agni Jātavedas</s>, you know them; may they rejoice in that offered svadhā; svadhā, homage. Whatever limb of yours the flesh-eating fire has burned, while <s>Jātavedas</s> was leading you to the worlds, that I restore to you again. Uninjured, come together with all your limbs, O fathers; svadhā, homage. Carry the ghee, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, to the fathers, wherever you know them to be placed far away. Let streams of ghee flow toward them; may their blessings be true with their desires; svadhā, homage.' In this same way he offers a second and likewise a third, adapting the mantra with 'to the grandfathers' and 'to the great-grandfathers.'

children.text: evamannasya juhoti vahānnam iti mantraṃ saṃnamati
children.translated_text: In the same way he offers some of the food, adapting the mantra with 'Carry the food.'

children.text: atha sauviṣṭakṛtīṃ juhoti agnaye kavyavāhanāya sviṣṭakṛte svadhā namaḥ iti
children.translated_text: Then he offers the <s>sauviṣṭakṛtī</s> oblation: 'To <s>Agni Kavyavāhana Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, svadhā, homage.'

children.text: athānnamabhimṛśati pṛthivī te pātraṃ dyaurapidhānaṃ brahmaṇastvā mukhe juhomi brāhmaṇānāṃ tvā prāṇāpānayorjuhomi akṣitamasi mā pit￣ṇāṃ kṣeṣṭhā amutrāmuṣmi￢lloke pṛthivī samā tasyāgnirupadraṣṭā dattasyāpramādāya pṛthivī te pātraṃ dyaurapidhānaṃ brahmaṇastvā mukhe juhomi brāhmaṇānāṃ tvā prāṇāpānayorjuhomi akṣitamasi mā pitāmahānāṃ kṣeṣṭhā amutrāmuṣmi￢lloke antarikṣaṃ samaṃ tasya vāyurupadraṣṭā dattasyāpramādāya pṛthivī te pātraṃ dyaurapidhānaṃ brahmaṇastvā mukhe juhomi brāhmaṇānāṃ tvā prāṇāpānayorjuhomi akṣitamasi mā prapitāmahānāṃ kṣeṣṭhā amutrāmuṣmi￢laloke dyauḥ samā tasyāditya upadraṣṭā dattasyāpramādāya iti brāhmaṇānupasparśayati
children.translated_text: Then he touches the food: 'Earth is your vessel, heaven your lid. I offer you into the mouth of <s>Brahman</s>; I offer you into the breaths, in-breath and out-breath, of the Brahmins. You are inexhaustible. Do not fail the fathers in that other world. Earth is equal; <s>Agni</s> is its overseer, for care over what has been given. Earth is your vessel, heaven your lid. I offer you into the mouth of <s>Brahman</s>; I offer you into the breaths, in-breath and out-breath, of the Brahmins. You are inexhaustible. Do not fail the grandfathers in that other world. The midspace is equal; <s>Vāyu</s> is its overseer, for care over what has been given. Earth is your vessel, heaven your lid. I offer you into the mouth of <s>Brahman</s>; I offer you into the breaths, in-breath and out-breath, of the Brahmins. You are inexhaustible. Do not fail the great-grandfathers in that other world. Heaven is equal; <s>Āditya</s> is its overseer, for care over what has been given.' Thus he has the Brahmins touch it.
'Having settled in the breath, I offer the immortal,' thus.
He looks at them as they are eating: 'My self is in <s>Brahman</s>, for immortality.'

children.text: bhuktavatonupravrajya śeṣamanujñāpyodakumbhaṃ darbhamuṣṭiṃ cādāya dakṣiṇapūrvamavāntaradeśaṃ gatvā dakṣiṇāgrāndarbhānsaṃstīrya teṣvavācīnapāṇirdakṣiṇāpavargāṃstrīnudakāñjalīnninayati mārjayantāṃ pitaraḥ somyāsaḥ mārjayantāṃ pitāmahāḥ somyāsaḥ mārjayantāṃ prapitāmahāḥ somyāsaḥ iti asāvavaneniṅkṣvāsāvavaneniṅkṣva iti vā
children.translated_text: After following those who have eaten, and after asking permission about the remainder, he takes a water-pot and a handful of darbha grass, goes to an intermediate place to the south-east, spreads darbha grass there with its tips to the south, and, with his hand turned downward, pours out three handfuls of water ending toward the south: 'May the Soma-drinking fathers cleanse themselves. May the Soma-drinking grandfathers cleanse themselves. May the Soma-drinking great-grandfathers cleanse themselves.' Or else: '<s>Asau</s>, wash yourself; <s>asau</s>, wash yourself.'

children.text: teṣvavācīnapāṇirdakṣiṇāpavargānpiṇḍāndadāti etatte tatāsau iti pitre piṇḍaṃ dadāti etatte pitāmahāsau iti pitāmahāya etatte prapitāmahāsau iti prapitāmahāya tūṣṇīṃ caturtham sa kṛtākṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: On those darbhas, with his hand turned downward, he places piṇḍas ending toward the south. Saying, 'This is for you, father <s>Asau</s>,' he gives the piṇḍa to the father; 'This is for you, grandfather <s>Asau</s>,' to the grandfather; 'This is for you, great-grandfather <s>Asau</s>,' to the great-grandfather. A fourth is silent; it is optional.

children.text: atha yadi nāmadheyāni na vindyāt svadhā pitṛbhyaḥ pṛthiviṣadbhyaḥ iti pitre piṇḍaṃ dadyāt svadhā pitṛbhyontarikṣasadbhyaḥ iti pitāmahāya svadhā pitṛbhyo diviṣadbhyaḥ iti prapitāmahāya
children.translated_text: Then, if he does not know their names, he should give the piṇḍa to the father with, 'Svadhā to the fathers who sit on earth'; to the grandfather with, 'Svadhā to the fathers who sit in the midspace'; and to the great-grandfather with, 'Svadhā to the fathers who sit in heaven.'
At this point he gives collyrium, unguent, and a garment along with each piṇḍa.
'Anoint yourself, <s>asau</s>; anoint yourself, <s>asau</s>,' thus he gives collyrium three times.
'Smear yourself, <s>asau</s>; smear yourself, <s>asau</s>,' thus he gives unguent three times.

children.text: etāni vaḥ pitaro vāsāṃsyato nonyatpitaro mā yūḍhvam iti daśāmūrṇāstukānvā chittvā nyasyati pūrve vayasi
children.translated_text: 'These, O fathers, are your garments; do not take anything else from us, O fathers.' Saying this, in the earlier age he cuts off and sets down the fringe or tufts of wool.
In the later age, he cuts off a piece from his own garment, because of greed.

children.text: atha pātraṃ saṃkṣālya putrānpautrānabhitarpayantīrāpo madhumatīrimāḥ svadhāṃ pitṛbhyo amṛtaṃ duhānāḥ āpo devīrubhayāṃstarpayantu nadīrimā udanvatīrvetasvinīḥ sutīrthyāḥ amuṣmi￢lloka upa vaḥ kṣrarantu iti prathavyaṃ pariṣicya nyubjapātraṃ pāṇī vyatyasya dakṣiṇamuttaramuttaraṃ ca dakṣiṇam namo vaḥ pitaro rasāya iti namaskārairupatiṣṭhate
children.translated_text: Then, after rinsing the vessel, with the waters satisfying sons and grandsons, sweet, milking immortality and svadhā for the fathers, 'May the divine waters satisfy both groups, these rivers rich in water, reed-filled, and with good fords. In that other world may they flow forth to you,' he sprinkles it around on the ground, turns the vessel mouth-down, crosses his hands, the right to the north and the left to the south, and worships with salutations: 'Homage to you, O fathers, for sap.'
Then, having gone to the edge of the water, he pours out three handfuls of water.

children.text: eṣa te tata madhumā￢ ūrmiḥ sarasvānyāvānagniśca pṛthivī ca tāvatyasya mātrā tāvānasya mahimā tāvantamenaṃ bhūtaṃ dadāmi yathāgnirakṣitonupadasta evaṃ mahyaṃ pitrekṣitonupadastaḥ svadhā bhavatāṃ taṃ svadhāmakṣitaṃ taiḥ sahopajīvāsāvṛcaste mahimā eṣa te pitāmaha madhumā￢ ūrmiḥ sarasvānyāvānvāyuścāntarikṣaṃ ca tāvatyasya mātrā tāvānasya mahimā tāvantamenaṃ bhūtaṃ dadāmi yathā vāyurakṣitonupadasta evaṃ mahyaṃ pitāmahāyākṣitonupadastaḥ svadhā bhavatāṃ taṃ svadhāmikṣitaṃ taiḥ sahopajīvāsau yajūṃṣi te mahimā eṣa te prapitāmaha madhumā￢ ūrmiḥ sarasvānyāvānādityaśca dyauśca tāvatyasya mātrā tāvānasya mahimā tāvantamenaṃ bhūtaṃ dadāmi yathādityokṣitonupadasta evaṃ mahyaṃ prapitāmahāyākṣitonupadastaḥ svadhā bhavatāṃ taṃ svadhāmakṣitaṃ taiḥ sahopajīvāsau sāmāni te mahimā iti
children.translated_text: 'This honeyed wave, rich in <s>Sarasvat</s>, is yours, father. As far as <s>Agni</s> and the earth extend, so great is its measure, so great its greatness. I give him, being such, to that extent. As <s>Agni</s> is undiminished and unexhausted, so may he be undiminished and unexhausted for me, for my father. May there be <s>svadhā</s>. May he live together with them on that undiminished <s>svadhā</s>. The ṛc-verses are your greatness. This honeyed wave, rich in <s>Sarasvat</s>, is yours, grandfather. As far as <s>Vāyu</s> and the atmosphere extend, so great is its measure, so great its greatness. I give him, being such, to that extent. As <s>Vāyu</s> is undiminished and unexhausted, so may he be undiminished and unexhausted for me, for my grandfather. May there be <s>svadhā</s>. May he live together with them on that undiminished <s>svadhā</s>. The yajus-formulas are your greatness. This honeyed wave, rich in <s>Sarasvat</s>, is yours, great-grandfather. As far as <s>Āditya</s> and heaven extend, so great is its measure, so great its greatness. I give him, being such, to that extent. As <s>Āditya</s> is undiminished and unexhausted, so may he be undiminished and unexhausted for me, for my great-grandfather. May there be <s>svadhā</s>. May he live together with them on that undiminished <s>svadhā</s>. The sāman-chants are your greatness.' Thus he says.

children.text: pratyetya pratiṣṭhitamudapātreṇopapravartayati parāyāta pitarah somyā gambhīraiḥ pathibhiḥ pūrvyaiḥ atha māsi punarāyāta no gṛhānhavirattuṃ suprajasaḥ suvīrāḥ iti
children.translated_text: Having returned, he sets the established thing in motion with the water vessel: 'Go away, O Soma-drinking fathers, by the deep ancient paths. Then, in a month, return again to our houses to eat the oblation, rich in offspring and rich in heroes.'
By this the rite at the middle of the rainy season has been explained.
There meat is prescribed.
If there is no meat, vegetables are used.
We shall explain the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>.
They call the eighth day of the latter fortnight following the full moon of <s>Māgha</s> the single <s>Aṣṭakā</s>.

children.text: tataḥ pūrvedyuranūrādheṣvaparāhṇegnimupasamādhāya dakṣiṇāprāgagnairdarbhaiḥ paristīryaikapavitrāntarhitāni catvāri vrīhiśarāvāṇi nirvapati imamapūpaṃ catuḥśarāvaṃ nirvapāmi kleśāvahaṃ pit￣ṇāṃ sāṃparāye devena savitrā prasūtaḥ devasya tvā savituḥ prasaveśvinorbāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ pitṛbhyaḥ pitāmahebhyaḥ prapitāmahebhyo vo juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi iti
children.translated_text: On the preceding day, under the Anūrādhās, in the afternoon, having laid the fire, strewn darbha grass with its tips to the south-east, he pours out four bowls of rice separated by a single purifier: 'I pour out this cake of four bowls, bringing hardship for the fathers in the next world, impelled by the god <s>Savitṛ</s>. At the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I pour you out, acceptable to the fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers.'

children.text: etenaiva pavitreṇa tūṣṇīṃ prokṣaṇīḥ saṃskṛtya tūṣṇīṃ prokṣya tūṣṇīmavahatya yathāpuroḍāśamevaṃ caturṣu kapāleṣu tūṣṇīṃ śrapayitvābhighāryodvāsya prasavyaṃ pariṣicyaudumbaramidhmamabhyādhāyaudumbaryā darvyopastirṇābhighāritaṃ dakṣiṇāprācīsaṃtataṃ paraṃparamavadāya dakṣiṇāprācīsaṃtataṃ paraṃparaṃ juhoti ulūkhalā grāvāṇo ghoṣamakrata haviḥ kṛṇvantaḥ parivatsarīṇām ekāṣṭake suprajā vīravanto vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇām svadhā namaḥ apūpaṃ deva ghṛtavantamagne svadhāvantaṃ pit￣ṇāṃ tarpaṇāya yathātathaṃ vaha havyamagne putraḥ pitṛbhya āhutiṃ juhomi svadhā namaḥ ayaṃ catuḥśarāvo ghṛtavānapūpaḥ payasvānagne rayimānpuṣṭimāṃśca pratinandantu pitaraḥ saṃvidānāḥ sviṣṭoyaṃ suhuto mamāstu svadhā namaḥ iti
children.translated_text: With that same purifier he silently prepares the sprinkling waters, silently sprinkles, silently pounds, and, as with a puroḍāśa cake, silently cooks it on four potsherds. Having sprinkled it with ghee, removed it from the fire, poured around it counterclockwise, put on udumbara fuel, and cut successive portions, continuous toward the south-east, from what has been spread under and sprinkled with ghee in an udumbara ladle, he offers the successive portions, continuous toward the south-east: 'The mortars and pressing-stones have made a sound, making the oblation of the yearly rites. At the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s> may we be rich in offspring and heroes, lords of wealth. <s>Svadhā</s>, homage. O god <s>Agni</s>, carry the ghee-filled cake, possessing <s>svadhā</s>, for the satisfaction of the fathers, in the proper way; O <s>Agni</s>, I, the son, offer the oblation to the fathers. <s>Svadhā</s>, homage. This four-bowl cake is filled with ghee, rich in milk, O <s>Agni</s>, rich in wealth and nourishment. May the fathers, agreeing together, rejoice in it. May this well-offered oblation be well sacrificed by me. <s>Svadhā</s>, homage.'

children.text: athānnasya juhoti iyameva sā yā prathamā vyauchat ekāṣṭakā tapasā tapyamānaā yā prathamā vyauchat iti
children.translated_text: Then he offers from the food: 'This indeed is she who first shone forth, the <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>, heating herself with austerity; she who first shone forth.'

children.text: apūpasyānnasyeti samavadāya sarpirmiśrasya juhoti agnaye kavyavāhanāya sviṣṭakṛte svadhā namaḥ iti
children.translated_text: Having taken equal portions of the cake and the food, mixed with ghee, he offers: 'To <s>Agni Kavyavāhana Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, <s>svadhā</s>, homage.'

children.text: taṃ ghṛtavantaṃ madhumantamannavantaṃ śrāddhābhimarśanenābhimṛśya piṇḍānāmāvṛtā piṇḍāndadāti
children.translated_text: Touching that ghee-filled, honeyed, food-filled offering with the śrāddha-touch, he gives the piṇḍas according to the rule for piṇḍas.
With it he serves learned Brahmins.
To them he gives food and wealth according to his faith.
The established gift of handfuls of water and the rest is as in the monthly rite.
On the following day he seizes a cow for the fathers.

children.text: agnimupasamādhāya dakṣiṇāprāgagrairdarbhaiḥ paristīrya imāṃ pitṛbhyo gāmupākaromi tāṃ me sametāḥ pitaro juṣantām medasvatīṃ ghṛtavatīṃ svadhāvatīṃ sā me pit￣nsāṃparāye dhinotu svadhā namaḥ ityupākaraṇīyāṃ hutvaikena barhiṣaikaśūlayā ca vapāśrapaṇyaudumbaryopākaroti pitṛbhyastvā juṣṭāmupākaromi iti
children.translated_text: Having laid the fire and strewn darbha grass with its tips to the south-east, he offers the preliminary oblation: 'I bring this cow near for the fathers. May my assembled fathers accept her, rich in fat, rich in ghee, possessing <s>svadhā</s>. May she satisfy my fathers in the next world. <s>Svadhā</s>, homage.' Then with one barhis grass, a single spit, a fat-cooking implement, and an udumbara branch he brings it near: 'I bring you near, acceptable to the fathers.'

children.text: athaināṃ prokṣati pitṛbhyastvā juṣṭāṃ prokṣāmi iti
children.translated_text: Then he sprinkles her: 'I sprinkle you, acceptable to the fathers.'

children.text: tāṃ prokṣitāṃ paryagni kṛtvā tāmapareṇāgniṃ pratyakśirasaṃ dakṣiṇāpadīṃ saṃjñapayanti
children.translated_text: Having sprinkled her and carried fire around her, they kill her west of the fire, with her head to the west and her feet to the south.

children.text: sajñaptāyai tūṣṇīmadbhiḥ prāṇānāpyāyya tūṣṇīṃ vapāṃ hṛdayaṃ matasne uddharati
children.translated_text: When she has been killed, he silently refreshes the breaths with water and silently takes out the fat, the heart, and the kidneys.

children.text: audumbaryā vapāśrapaṇyā vapāṃ śrapayatyaudumbareṣu śūleṣu pṛthagitarāṇi
children.translated_text: He cooks the fat with an udumbara fat-cooking implement, and the other parts separately on udumbara spits.

children.text: śrapayitvābhighāryodvāsya prasavyaṃ pariṣicyaudumbaramidhmamabhyādhāyaudumbaryā darvyopastīrṇābhighāritāṃ vapāṃ juhoti vaha vapāṃ jātavedaḥ pitṛbhyo yatraitānvettha nihitānparāke medasaḥ kūlyā upa tānkṣarantu satyā eṣāmāśiṣaḥ santu kāmaiḥ svadhā namaḥ iti
children.translated_text: Having cooked it, sprinkled it with ghee, removed it from the fire, poured around counterclockwise, put on udumbara fuel, and spread under and sprinkled the fat with ghee in an udumbara ladle, he offers it: 'Carry the fat, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, to the fathers, where you know them to be placed far away. Let streams of fat flow to them; may their true blessings be fulfilled according to their desires. <s>Svadhā</s>, homage.'
He offers the fat as an all-offering. Having drawn out the remainder, he should feed the Brahmins.

children.text: upasthitenna odanasya māṃsānāmiti samavadāya sarpirmiśrasya juhoti ekāṣṭakāṃ paśyata dohamānāmannaṃ māṃsavadghṛtavatsvadhāvat tadbrāhmaṇairatipūtamannaṃtamakṣitaṃ tanme astu svadhā namaḥ ekāṣṭakā tapasā tapyamānā saṃvatsarasya patnī duduhe prapīnā taṃ dohamupajīvātha pitaraḥ saṃvidānāḥ sviṣṭoyaṃ suhuto mamāstu svadhā namaḥ saṃvatsarasya pratimām iti
children.translated_text: Having cut off portions from the rice and meat that are present, he offers it mixed with ghee: 'Behold <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>, who is being milked, food with meat, with ghee, with <s>svadhā</s>. That food, exceedingly purified by the Brahmins, that imperishable food, may it be mine. <s>Svadhā</s>, homage. <s>Ekāṣṭakā</s>, heated with heat, the wife of the year, full-uddered, has milked. Live upon that milk, O fathers, being in accord. May this be well-offered and well-sacrificed by me. <s>Svadhā</s>, homage. The image of the year,' and so on.

children.text: hutvānnasya māṃsānāmiti samavadāya sarpirmiśrasya juhoti agnaye kavyavāhanāya sviṣṭakṛte svadhā namaḥ iti
children.translated_text: Having offered, he cuts off portions from the food and meat and offers them mixed with ghee: 'To <s>Agni Kavyavāhana Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, <s>svadhā</s>, homage.'
The giving of handfuls of water and the rest is as prescribed, as in the monthly rite.
But here the gifts of food and wealth are not fixed.

children.text: śvobhūte māṃsaśeṣeṇa pitṛbhyonnaṃ saṃskṛtya tvamagne ayāsi prajāpate iti juhoti
children.translated_text: On the following day, having prepared food for the fathers with the remainder of the meat, he offers with 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are ayās,' and 'O <s>Prajāpati</s>.'
The giving of handfuls of water and the rest is as prescribed, as in the monthly rite.
Now then, the Śravaṇa rite.
On the full-moon day that is joined with the lunar mansion <s>Śravaṇa</s>, after the evening agnihotra he lays the southern fire; one who has not established the sacred fires uses the domestic fire.
Then he prepares unbroken grains, unbroken parched grains, flour, kiṃśuka flowers, collyrium and anointing substance, and ghee.

children.text: darvyāmupastīryaiteṣāmevānnānāṃ samavadāya sarpirmiśrasya juhoti namognaye pārthivāya pārthivānāmadhipataye svāhā namo vāyave vibhumata āntarikṣāṇāmadhipataye svāhā namaḥ sūryāya rohitāya divyānāmadhipataye svāhā namo viṣṇave gaurāya diśyānāmadhipataye svāhā iti
children.translated_text: Having spread ghee in the ladle, he cuts off portions from these very foods and offers them mixed with ghee: 'Homage to <s>Agni</s>, the earthly one, lord of earthly beings, svāhā. Homage to <s>Vāyu Vibhumat</s>, lord of atmospheric beings, svāhā. Homage to <s>Sūrya Rohita</s>, lord of heavenly beings, svāhā. Homage to <s>Viṣṇu Gaura</s>, lord of beings of the directions, svāhā.'

children.text: kiṃśukānyājyena saṃyujya juhoti jagdho maśako jagdhā vicaṣṭirjagdho vyadhvaraḥ jagdho vyadhvaro jagdhā vicaṣṭirjagdho maśakaḥ jagdhā vicaṣṭirjagdho maśako jagdho vyadhvaraḥ iti
children.translated_text: Having combined the kiṃśuka flowers with ghee, he offers: 'The mosquito has been eaten, the vicaṣṭi has been eaten, the vyadhvara has been eaten. The vyadhvara has been eaten, the vicaṣṭi has been eaten, the mosquito has been eaten. The vicaṣṭi has been eaten, the mosquito has been eaten, the vyadhvara has been eaten.'

children.text: udakumbhaṃ darbhamuṣṭiṃ cādāya prāṅmukho niṣkramya prāco darbhānsaṃstīrya teṣu caturo balīnharati ye pārthivāḥ sarpāstebhya imaṃ baliṃ harāmi ya āntarikṣāḥ ye divyaḥ ye diśyāḥ iti
children.translated_text: Taking a water jar and a handful of darbha grass, he goes out facing east, spreads darbha grass toward the east, and on it presents four bali offerings: 'Those serpents that are earthly, to them I present this bali; those that are atmospheric; those that are heavenly; those that belong to the directions.'

children.text: atrāñjanābhyañjane dattvopatiṣṭhate namo astu sarpebhyaḥ ityetairmantraiḥ
children.translated_text: Having given the collyrium and anointing substance there, he worships with the mantras beginning 'Homage be to the serpents.'

children.text: udakumbhamādāya triḥ pradakṣiṇamāvasathaṃ pariṣiñcanparikrāmedyāvatā kāmayetaitāvatā me sarpā nāvakrāmeyuriti apa śveta padā jahi pūrveṇa cāpareṇa ca sapta ca mānuṣīrimāstisraśca rājabandhavaiḥ na vai śvetasyābhyācareṇāhirjaghāna kaṃ cana śvetāya vaidarvāya namo namaḥ śvetāya vaidarvāya iti
children.translated_text: Taking the water jar, he should go around the dwelling three times clockwise, sprinkling it, saying, 'As far as I desire, so far may the serpents not creep upon me.' Then: 'Strike away with the white foot, both with the former and the latter; these seven human women and three with royal kinsmen. By the transgression of the white one, no serpent ever killed anyone. Homage, homage to <s>Śveta Vaidarva</s>; to <s>Śveta Vaidarva</s>.'

children.text: athopatiṣṭhate samīcī nāmāsi prācī dik ityetairmantraiḥ pratidiśam
children.translated_text: Then he worships in each direction with the mantras beginning, 'You are named <s>Samīcī</s>, the eastern direction.'
From then onward he presents the bali regularly until the Mārgaśīrṣa full moon.
There is no kiṃśuka offering here.
No sprinkling is prescribed.
He presents the bali offerings at the end with 'I shall set down, I shall set down.'
We shall explain the Āgrahāyaṇī rite.

children.text: mārgaśīrṣyāṃ paurṇamāsyāmagnimupasamādhāya saṃparistīrya payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvābhighāryodvāsya vyāhṛtiparyantaṃ kṛtvā juhoti iḍāyai sṛptaṃ ghṛtavaccarācaraṃ jātavedo haviridaṃ juṣasva ye grāmyāḥ paśavo viśvarūpāsteṣāṃ saptānāmiha rantirastu puṣṭiḥ svāhā yāṃ janāḥ pratinandanti rātriṃ dhenumivāyatīm saṃvatsarasya yā patnī sā no astu sumaṅgalī svāhā śivā paśubhyo dārebhyaḥ śivā naktaṃ śivā divā saṃvatsarasya yā patnī sā no astu sumaṅgalī svāhā paurṇamāsī pūrayantyāyāntyaparāparān māsārdhamāsānvibhajati sā naḥ pūrṇābhirakṣatu svāhā iti
children.translated_text: On the full moon of Mārgaśīrṣa, having laid the fire, strewn it round, cooked a rice mess in milk, sprinkled it with ghee, taken it from the fire, and performed the rite up to the vyāhṛtis, he offers: 'What has crept for <s>Iḍā</s>, moving and unmoving, rich in ghee, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, enjoy this oblation. Of the village animals, multiform, may there be here delight and nourishment for those seven, svāhā. The night which people welcome, like a milch cow as she approaches, she who is the wife of the year, may she be auspicious for us, svāhā. Auspicious for the cattle and for the wives, auspicious by night, auspicious by day; she who is the wife of the year, may she be auspicious for us, svāhā. The full moon, filling up, coming again and again, divides the months and half-months; may she, full, protect us, svāhā.'

children.text: atha sauviṣṭakṛtīṃ juhoti sviṣṭamagne abhi tatpṛṇāhi viśvā deva pṛtanā abhiṣya uruṃ naḥ panthāṃ pradiśanvibhāhi jyotiṣmaddhehyajaraṃ na āyuḥ iti
