children.translated_text: Then he offers the <s>sauviṣṭakṛtī</s> oblation: 'What has been well sacrificed, O <s>Agni</s>, fill that out. O god, overcome all hostile forces; showing us a broad path, shine forth. Bestow on us a luminous, undecaying life.'

children.text: tataḥ pāṇī prakṣālya bhūmimālabhate prati kṣatre pratitiṣṭhāmi rāṣṭre pratyaśveṣu pratitiṣṭhāmi goṣu pratyaṅgeṣu pratitiṣṭhāmyātmanprati prāṇeṣu pratitiṣṭhāmi puṣṭe prati dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ pratitiṣṭhāmi yajñe trayā devā ekādaśa trayastriṃśāḥ surādhasaḥ bṛhaspatipurohitā devasya savituḥ save devā devairavantu mā iti
children.translated_text: Then, having washed his hands, he touches the earth: 'I stand firm in power; I stand firm in the kingdom; I stand firm among horses; I stand firm among cows; I stand firm in my limbs; I stand firm in myself; I stand firm in the vital breaths; I stand firm in nourishment; I stand firm in heaven and earth; I stand firm in the sacrifice. The three and eleven and thirty-three gods, rich in good gifts, with <s>Bṛhaspati</s> as priest, at the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, may the gods protect me together with the gods.'
Of them, the householder sits down on the southern side.
The others sit successively farther to the north.
According to the order of the production of offspring.
Among them, those who know the mantras recite those mantras.

children.text: syonā pṛthivi bhavānṛkṣarā niveśanī yacchā naḥ śarma saprathāḥ baḍitthā parvatānām iti dvābhyāṃ dakṣiṇaiḥ pārśvaiḥ saṃviśanti
children.translated_text: With the two verses, 'Be pleasant, O earth, thornless, a dwelling place; grant us shelter, broad and wide,' and 'Baḍ itthā of the mountains,' they lie down on their right sides.
They rise with 'With rising life.'
Having risen, they recite, 'We have risen; we have become immortal.'
Thus they come together three times during the night.

children.text: rāhmaṇānannena pariviṣya puṇyāhaṃ svastyayanamṛddhimiti vācayitvāthaitāṃ rātriṃ vasanti ||
children.translated_text: Having served the Brahmins with food and had them pronounce, 'An auspicious day, welfare, and prosperity,' they then spend that night there.
Now then, we shall explain the rites of taking up and laying aside.

children.text: śravaṇāpakṣa oṣadhīṣu jātāsu hastena paurṇamāsyāṃ vādhyāyopākarma
children.translated_text: When the herbs have appeared in the fortnight of <s>Śravaṇa</s>, on the full-moon day under <s>Hasta</s>, there is the taking up of study.

children.text: agnimupasamādhāya vyāhṛtiparyantaṃ kṛtvā kāṇḍarṣīñjuhoti prajāpataye kāṇḍarṣaye svāhā somāya kāṇḍarṣaye svāhā agnaye kāṇḍarṣaye svāhā viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ kāṇḍarṣibhyaḥ svāhā svayaṃbhuve kāṇḍarṣaye svāhā iti kāṇḍarṣayaḥ kāṇḍanāmāni vā sāvitrīmṛgvedaṃ yajurvedaṃ sāmavedamatharvavedaṃ sadasaspatimiti
children.translated_text: Having laid the fire and performed the rite up to the vyāhṛtis, he offers to the kāṇḍarṣis: 'To <s>Prajāpati</s>, the kāṇḍarṣi, svāhā; to <s>Soma</s>, the kāṇḍarṣi, svāhā; to <s>Agni</s>, the kāṇḍarṣi, svāhā; to all the gods, the kāṇḍarṣis, svāhā; to <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, the kāṇḍarṣi, svāhā.' These are the kāṇḍarṣis. Or he offers the names of the sections: the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, and <s>Sadasaspati</s>.
Having offered, they study the first three anuvākas from the beginning.
Or all the beginnings of the sections.
He proceeds with the rites beginning with the jaya-offerings.

children.text: sviṣṭakṛdantaṃ kṛtvā tryahamekāhaṃ vā kṣamya yathādhyāyamadhyetavyamiti vadanti
children.translated_text: Having performed the rite up to the sviṣṭakṛt, after abstaining for three days or one day, they say that one should study according to the lesson.
In the fortnight of <s>Taiṣa</s>, under <s>Rohiṇī</s>, or on the full-moon day, there is the laying aside.

children.text: sagaṇaḥ prācīmudīcīṃ vā diśamupaniṣkramya yatrāpaḥ sukhāḥ sukhāvagāhāstadavagāhyāghamarṣaṇena trīnprāṇāyāmānkṛtvā sapavitraiḥ pāṇibhiḥ āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvaḥ iti tisṛbhiḥ hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ iti catasṛbhiḥ pavamānaḥ suvarjanaḥ iti caitenānuvākena snātvā darbhānanyonyasmai saṃprayacchanto ditsanta ivānyonyam
children.translated_text: Together with his group he goes out toward the east or north. Where the waters are pleasant and easy to enter, having entered them and performed three breath-restraints with the Aghamarṣaṇa hymn, he bathes with hands holding pavitras, using the three verses beginning 'O waters, you are bringers of refreshment,' the four verses beginning 'Golden-colored, pure, purifying,' and this anuvāka beginning 'The purifier, winning heaven'; then, holding darbha grass, they hand it to one another as if wishing to give it to one another.

children.text: tataḥ śucau deśe prācīnapravaṇe prāgagrairdarbhairudagapavargāṇyāsanāni kalpayanti ||
children.translated_text: Then, in a clean place sloping eastward, they prepare seats of darbha grass with the tips eastward, ending toward the north.

children.text: brahmane prajāpataye bṛhaspatayegnaye vāyave sūryāya candramase nakṣatrebhya indrāya rājñe yamāya rājñe varuṇāya rājñe somāya rājñe vaiśravaṇāya rājñe vasubhyo rudrebhya ādityebhyo viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ sādhyebhya ṛbhubhyo bhṛgubhyo marudbhyotharvabhyoṅgirobhya iti devagaṇānām
children.translated_text: For <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Candramas</s>, the lunar mansions, <s>Indra</s> the king, <s>Yama</s> the king, <s>Varuṇa</s> the king, <s>Soma</s> the king, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> the king, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Ādityas</s>, all the gods, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, the <s>Atharvans</s>, and the <s>Aṅgirases</s>: thus for the hosts of gods.

children.text: viśvāmitro jamadagnirbharadvājotha gautamaḥ atrirvasiṣṭhaḥ kaśyapaḥ ityete saptarṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Jamadagni</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and <s>Kaśyapa</s>: these are the seven seers.

children.text: nivītina uttarata udīcīnapravaṇa udagagrairdarbhaiḥ prāgapavargāṇyāsanāni kalpayanti viśvāmitrāya jamadagnaye bharadvājāya gautamāyātraye vasiṣṭhāya kaśyapāya
children.translated_text: Wearing the nivīta, to the north, on ground sloping northward, with darbha grass whose tips point north, they prepare seats ending toward the east, for <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Jamadagni</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and <s>Kaśyapa</s>.
In the space between <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s> they prepare one for <s>Arundhatī</s>.
To the south, on ground sloping eastward, they prepare one for <s>Agastya</s>.

children.text: tata ekavedyāntebhyaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanāya jātūkarṇyāya tarukṣāya tṛṇabindave varmiṇe varūthine vājine vājaśravase satyaśravase suśravase sutaśravase somaśuṣmāyaṇāya satvavate bṛhadukthāya vāmadevāya vājiratnāya haryajvāyanāyodamayāya gautamāya ṛṇaṃjayāya ṛtaṃjayāya kṛtaṃjayāya dhanaṃjayāya babhrave tryaruṇāya trivarṣāya tridhātave śibintāya parāśarāya viṣṇave rudrāya skandāya kāśīśvarāya śvarāya dharmāyārthāya kāmāya krodhāya vasiṣṭhāyendrāya tvaṣṭre kartre dhartre dhātre mṛtyave savitre sāvitryai vedebhyaśca pṛthakpṛthagṛgvedāya yajurvedāya sāmavedāyātharvavedāyetihāsapurāṇāyeti
children.translated_text: Then, from the end of the same altar, separately for each, they prepare seats for <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>, <s>Jātūkarṇya</s>, <s>Tarukṣa</s>, <s>Tṛṇabindu</s>, <s>Varmin</s>, <s>Varūthin</s>, <s>Vājin</s>, <s>Vājaśravas</s>, <s>Satyaśravas</s>, <s>Suśravas</s>, <s>Sutaśravas</s>, <s>Somaśuṣmāyaṇa</s>, <s>Satvavat</s>, <s>Bṛhaduktha</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Vājiratna</s>, <s>Haryajvāyana</s>, <s>Udamaya</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Ṛṇaṃjaya</s>, <s>Ṛtaṃjaya</s>, <s>Kṛtaṃjaya</s>, <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, <s>Babhru</s>, <s>Tryaruṇa</s>, <s>Trivarṣa</s>, <s>Tridhātu</s>, <s>Śibinta</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Kāśīśvara</s>, <s>Śvara</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Artha</s>, <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Krodha</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Kartṛ</s>, <s>Dhartṛ</s>, <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Mṛtyu</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Sāvitrī</s>, and for the Vedas separately: for the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, and for Itihāsa and Purāṇa.

children.text: dakṣiṇataḥ prācīnāvītino dakṣiṇāpravaṇe dakṣiṇāgrairdarbhaiḥ pratyagapavargāṇyāsanāni kalpayanti ||
children.translated_text: To the south, wearing the sacred cord over the right shoulder, on ground sloping southward, with darbha grass whose tips point south, they prepare seats ending toward the west.

children.text: vaiśampāyanāya paliṅgave tittirāyokhāyātreyāya padakārāya kauṇḍiṇyāya vṛttikārāya sūtrakārebhyaḥ satyāṣāḍhāya pravacanakartṛbhya ācāryebhya ṛṣibhyo vānaprasthebhya ūrdhvaretobhya ekapatnībhya iti
children.translated_text: For <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>, <s>Paliṅgava</s>, <s>Tittiri</s>, <s>Ukha</s>, <s>Ātreya</s>, the maker of the pada-text, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, the maker of the vṛtti, the makers of the sūtras, <s>Satyāṣāḍha</s>, the makers of the teaching, the teachers, the seers, the forest-dwellers, those who keep their seed upward, and those with one wife.
They prepare seats for their own ancestors and maternal grandfathers.
With a seat he says, 'For this one I prepare it, for this one I prepare it.'
With water he says, 'This one I satisfy, this one I satisfy.'
With perfume, flowers, incense, and lamps he says, 'Homage to this one, homage to this one.'
With food he says, 'To this one, svāhā; to this one, svāhā.'
With fruit-water he says, 'This one I satisfy, this one I satisfy.'
Having worshiped them, he says, 'Homage to this one, homage to this one.'

children.text: apareṇa vedimagnimupasamādhāya vyāhṛtiparyantaṃ kṛtvā kāṇḍarṣīñjuhoti kāṇḍanāmāni vā sāvitrīmṛgvedaṃ yajurvedaṃ sāmavedamatharvavedaṃ sadasaspatimiti hutvā prathamenānuvākenādhīyate kāṇḍādīnvā sarvān jayādi pratipadyate sviṣṭakṛdantaṃ kṛtvā tryahamekāhaṃ vā kṣamya yathādhyāyamadhyetavyamiti vadanti
children.translated_text: West of the altar, having laid the fire and performed the rite up to the vyāhṛtis, he offers to the kāṇḍarṣis, or else the names of the sections: the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, and <s>Sadasaspati</s>. Having offered, he studies with the first anuvāka, or all the beginnings of the sections. He proceeds with the rites beginning with the jaya-offerings. Having performed the rite up to the sviṣṭakṛt, after abstaining for three days or one day, they say that one should study according to the lesson.

children.text: kāṇḍātkāṇḍāt yā śatena iti dvābhyāmudakānte dūrvā ropayanti
children.translated_text: At the edge of the water they plant dūrvā grass with the two formulas 'From section to section' and 'With a hundred.'

children.text: udadhimūrmimantaṃ kṛtvā prācīmudīcīṃ vā diśamātamitorājiṃ dhāvanti
children.translated_text: Having made the ocean wavy, they run in a line as far as it extends toward the east or north.
Having returned, they satisfy the Brahmins with cakes, barley-meal, and boiled rice.
At the completion of a pārāyaṇa it is the same, except for the planting of dūrvā grass and the running to the ocean.
Daily, with water alone, they satisfy the gods, the seers, and the ancestors; they satisfy them.
